# Vendored `gpui-component`

This directory starts from the complete published `gpui-component` 0.7.3 crate. It is vendored so DBFlux can adapt the editor's find/replace panel and the component key bindings to its keyboard-first navigation.

- Upstream: [`gpui-component` 0.7.3 on crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/gpui-component/0.7.3), from the crates.io registry archive `gpui-component-0.7.3.crate`.
- License: Apache-2.0; see `LICENSE-APACHE` and the published `Cargo.toml`.
- Archive SHA-256: `465a363235cd4062ef5f0953fc096fc764ed6f53dfbd9f409f669f93ea3b1ff9` (the checksum the crates.io index records for 0.7.3).

## Local patch list

Every local change is listed here with the file it touches and the behaviour it changes.

- `src/input/overlay.rs` and `src/input/search.rs`: when the overlay sync sees the search session close, it returns focus to the editor only if the panel's search or replace field still has focus (`SearchPanel::has_focus`). Upstream refocused the editor unconditionally, which took focus back from wherever it had moved when the session closed after focus left the panel, for example a pane move out of the find panel while a language-feature popover kept the overlay host alive. Closing from inside the panel (Escape, the close button) still returns focus to the editor. The crate's own tests never apply overlay focus (`!cfg!(test)`), so this path has no test here.
- `src/input/search.rs`: `SearchPanel::cycle_focus` calls `cx.propagate()` when the replace row is hidden or the editor is not replaceable, so Tab and Shift+Tab fall through to the next key binding (DBFlux's workspace pane cycle) instead of being consumed with no effect. Upstream kept Tab inside the panel even when it had a single field, which left no keyboard way out of the find panel other than Escape. With the replace row shown, Tab still moves between the search and replace fields. Covered by `tab_in_the_find_panel_cycles_panes_unless_the_replace_row_is_shown` in `crates/dbflux_ui_document/src/code/vim/tests.rs`.
- `Cargo.toml`: the `[package.metadata.cargo-machete]` `ignored` list adds `log`. CI runs `cargo machete` over the whole directory tree, so it analyses this crate too, and the published crate declares `log` without using it (it logs through `tracing`). Removing the dependency would change the published manifest more than exempting it.
- `src/highlighter/registry.rs` and `src/highlighter/wasm_stub.rs`: `SyntaxColors` gains the slots `field`, `namespace`, `type.alias`, `variable.alias` and `variable.column_alias`, each with its arm in `SyntaxColors::style`. DBFlux's SQL highlight query captures columns, schemas, alias qualifiers, declared table aliases and column aliases under these names, and the palette styles them. Upstream has no slot for them, so the captures fell back to their prefix (`type`, `variable`) or to no style at all. Covered by `sql_captures_give_each_identifier_its_role` in `crates/dbflux_components/src/highlighting.rs` and `syntax_roles_are_styled_in_both_variants` in `crates/dbflux_components/src/theme.rs`.
- `src/input/popovers/completion_menu.rs` and `Cargo.toml`: the completion menu highlights the characters of each label that fuzzy-match the item's `filter_text` (fzf-style, through `fuzzy-matcher`'s skim matcher, case-insensitive), instead of the first `filter_text.len()` characters. DBFlux's SQL completion offers fuzzy matches such as `alarm_message` for `messa`, where a leading-prefix highlight marks the wrong letters. Prefix matches highlight exactly as before. The manifest adds the `fuzzy-matcher` 0.3 dependency the workspace already uses.
- `src/input/popovers/completion_menu.rs`: each completion response shortlists at most 32 rows with the most characters in their labels plus details, measures those rows at their natural width including popover padding, and uses the widest measured row for the menu's explicit content width. A bounded heap keeps candidate storage constant, and expensive layout calls are bounded even when prefix matches contain thousands of tables; all suggestions remain available. The shortlist is a heuristic for proportional fonts, rather than a guarantee of finding the widest row in an arbitrary list. The width is capped by `Lsp::completion_menu.max_width` and the space to the right of the caret. The virtual list measures against its previous viewport width, so relying on intrinsic sizing kept later long suggestions as narrow as an earlier short response. Measurement happens when items change, rather than on every render. DBFlux sets the cap to 640 px. Covered by the candidate-bound and Unicode/detail tests in this file, and `completion_menu_fits_long_labels_and_caps_its_width` in `crates/dbflux_ui_document/src/code/vim/tests.rs`. `src/input/overlay.rs` includes an ignored `completion_menu_large_response_performance` test for manual response-to-frame comparisons at 100, 1,000 and 10,000 items.
- `src/input/input.rs`: synchronize overlays under the input's text-style refinement. Completion rows are measured during synchronization, before the input container is laid out; without this scope they used the surrounding UI font rather than the editor's font and spacing, underestimating filtered table labels. Covered by `completion_menu_keeps_table_labels_visible_while_typing` in `src/input/overlay.rs`, using typed prefixes and explicit editor letter spacing to make the measurement mismatch observable in headless tests.
- `src/select.rs`: the trigger shows the committed selection's title rather than the item under the list cursor, so moving the cursor through a filtered search does not change the shown value until Enter. While the list is open and has rows but no highlighted row, the first match is highlighted (`highlight_first_match_if_unset`), so Enter picks a match right after a query that went from no matches to some; the list decides the highlight from the rows it last drew, which are none after an empty result. 0.7.3 itself now clears the query and resolves the committed value in the full list on every close, which the 0.6.1 copy patched locally.

## Refresh

Retrieve the desired published `.crate` archive into the Cargo registry cache, verify its SHA-256 against the registry checksum in `Cargo.lock` (or the crates.io index for a new version), and stop if it differs. Extract the archive's single versioned root into `vendor/gpui-component/`, retaining its manifest, license, and source files. Keep the root `[patch.crates-io]` entry and resolve the lockfile with Cargo; check the diff against the published archive to identify every local deviation. Run `cargo check -p dbflux_ui_document` and `cargo nextest run -p dbflux_ui_document` after refreshing. A version change requires revalidating every local patch against the new published source.
